stemBlocks.value: One card is selected at random from a standard pack of 52 playing cards, containing 13 cards in each of hearts, diamonds, clubs and spades. (a) State the number of outcomes in the sample space. (b) Find the probability that the card is red. (c) Find the probability that the card is a king. (d) Find the probability that the card is a red queen. (e) Find the probability that the card is not a spade.
Think first: Recall how a pack is built: four suits of 13, two red and two black, with four cards of each rank.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p088-q17 from workbook page 88.

solutionSteps.instruction: Count the cards in the pack.

contentBlocks.value: One king in each suit, so 4/52
Queen of hearts and queen of diamonds only, so 2/52

solutionSteps.instruction: Use the complement for 'not a spade'.

strategyBlocks.value: Count the favourable cards in each case out of 52 and simplify; for 'not a spade' the complement is quicker than counting the other three suits.

whyThisWorks.value: Every card is equally likely, so each probability is the number of cards fitting the description divided by 52. When an event is defined by what it is not, the complement rule P(not A) = 1 − P(A) replaces a long count with a single subtraction.

commonErrors.misconception: Counting 4 red queens instead of 2 — only hearts and diamonds are red.
